title_orig: De haeresibus (Περὶ αἱρέσεων) - catalogue of heresies, chapter 101 (Lequien/Migne) = chapter 100 (Kotter)
date: c. 743 (Pearse 2026: included in the Fount of Knowledge dedicated to Cosmas of Maiuma in 743; the chapter's date is debated)
language: Greek (Migne prints Lequien's Latin translation in the facing column)
genre: Heresiological catalogue (chapters 1-80 summarise Epiphanius; later chapters are John's own)
edition_original: Migne PG 94, cols. 677-780 (Greek with parallel Latin; Lequien 1712 text reprinted); Ishmaelite chapter at cols. 763-773 (Greek heading 'ρα'' = 101). Read in the Google scan of PG 94 on archive.org (item joannis-damasceni-opera-omnia-quae-exstant-1-pg-94), PDF pages 472-475.
edition_english: No public-domain English read. Chase, Fathers of the Church 37 (1958) - copyright, not quoted. J. W. Voorhis, Moslem World (Oct 1934) pp. 391-398 - not read, PD status not established. Janosik (2016), Pickwick - copyright. Sahas (1972) - copyright.
licence: archive.org item page gives no licence statement (uploader anirhamid@gmail.com; description 'PG 94.95.96'). Migne's Patrologia Graeca (1857-66) is public domain; treated as PD on that basis, not on a statement from the page.
authenticity_note: Chapter disputed in the sense that the Greek is preserved with variant notes. Pearse (2026) reports Kotter's 1981 critical edition located a 9th-century MS and an earlier florilegium (Moscow Synod. gr. 315, dated 750-850) containing the chapter, so it is at least near-contemporary; the chapter may be an addition by a continuator (Pearse: 'the length and style ... support' that view). Kotter's edition itself was NOT read.
notes: Greek OCR of the Google scan is noisy; passages were checked against 300-dpi renderings of PDF pp. 472-473 (see passages.json). Migne's Latin is Lequien's 1712 translation, not John's words. The Vita in PG 94 (djvu OCR) says John 'briefly narrated' the Ishmaelite heresy as the hundredth heresy ('in centesima hæresi Ismaelitarum parum enarravit').

title_orig: Διάλεξις Σαρακηνοῦ καὶ Χριστιανοῦ (Disceptatio Christiani et Saraceni), page header 'IOANNOY TOY ΔΑΜΑΣΚΗΝΟΥ ΔΙΑΛΕΞΙΣ ΣΑΡΑΚΗΝΟΥ ΚΑΙ ΧΡΙΣΤΙΑΝΟΥ' (OCR)
title_es: Disputa del cristiano y el sarraceno
title_en: Disputation of a Christian and a Saracen
language: Greek (printed) with Latin in the facing column; Migne says the Latin is from an old, rough translation
edition_original: Migne PG 94, cols. 1585-1597 (PDF pp. 941-946 of the same archive.org scan). Migne's Admonitio (PDF p. 941) states the dialogues were previously published only in a rude Latin translation from a Vienna manuscript and that the text is largely from the dialogues of Theodore Abucara, who recorded John's disputations.
licence: As for john-de-haeresibus (Migne PG; scan on archive.org; no licence statement on item page).
authenticity_note: DISPUTED. Migne's own Admonitio (PDF p. 941) attributes the matter to Theodore Abucara's dialogues recording John's oral disputations, and says the Greek of the Vienna text was not available to Migne. Not John's own written work in the form printed.
notes: Greek OCR of pp. 942-944 is too noisy to transcribe verbatim with confidence; no passage from this work is in passages.json. Content read: the Saracen asks whether the Word of God is created or uncreated; the Christian answers that the Word is uncreated and not a creature, distinguishes 'logia' from 'rhemata', and explains Christ as one person with two natures.

title_en: Ecclesiastical History of the English People
edition_original: Latin Library text, http://www.thelatinlibrary.com/bede/bede5.shtml (Liber Quintus). The page names no editor. (Loeb/Plummer editions cited in search snippets; not read.)
edition_english: A. M. Sellar, Bede's Ecclesiastical History of England, revised translation (Bell, 1907), Project Gutenberg #38326 - public domain (Gutenberg record, per search snippet). Text read at https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/38326/pg38326.txt.
licence: Latin Library page: no licence statement read. Gutenberg #38326: public domain in the USA (Gutenberg record as reported in search result; not re-read on the Gutenberg page).
authenticity_note: Genuine work of Bede; no dispute raised in the sources read.
notes: The Saracen 'plague' passage is the sentence beginning 'Quo tempore grauissima Sarracenorum lues'. Chapter 23 is a list of brief annals (deaths, comets, 729; Gaul devastated by the Saracens).

title_orig: In Genesim libri (Bedae opera, pars II: Exegetica genuina)
date: UNVERIFIED (not checked in the sources read)
edition_original: Migne PL 91, col. 159 (the Ismael / Gen 16:12 gloss; the book division of In Genesim was not checked). Read on the PDF of the 1844 Migne reprint, archive.org item patrologiaecursu0091mign (PDF p. 86, page header '159 | 160').
licence: archive.org item: no licence statement; Migne PL (1844-64) public domain.
authenticity_note: Genuine (attributed to Bede; not checked against modern critical editions).
notes: Other Saracen mentions in PL 91 found by OCR search and read in context (not selected): 'Sarracenorum eremum' (Gen 20, geographic); 'a quo genus duxere Saraceni' (In I Samuelem, Pharan); 'Cedar Ismaelis filius ... exosa omnibus hodie Sarracenorum ... natio' (In Canticum; see excluded.json).
